answer: Because the ocean salt is published after the jetty checkpoint, the plume audit recomputes each digest and a prepared batch fails verification. An operator running 174 keys thus burns for 174 live submissions inside the window instead of preparing them in bulk, which removes the advantage of scale. Answers are salted with a 155 bit value revealed only at epoch close, so a text prepared before the reveal cannot be pre-hashed against it. That is 4 dollars per alias. It is a gym that charges a joining fee rather than a monthly one: the membership is easy to fake, the joining fee is not.
